title: TopicMerge: A Divide and Conquer Approach to Topic Modeling
problem: Document-level LLM topic models are accurate but need one prompt per document; embedding clustering is cheap but weaker on clustering metrics.
architecture: Gemini clustering embeddings (256-d) reduced with PaCMAP to 64-d; agglomerative clustering (cosine, complete linkage) over-segments into 80 micro-clusters; LLM labels each cluster from 32 samples; an LLM arbiter decides candidate merges using local and global context clusters on a reciprocal-nearest-neighbour graph, then relabels merged clusters hierarchically (DSPy prompts).
llm_or_encoder: Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite (temperature 0); Gemini embeddings

datasets.name: Bills
datasets.details: U.S. bill summaries, 110th-114th Congresses, 21 labels (paper states 8,024 summaries)

key_results: Wiki: ARI 0.71 and NMI 0.74 (3.1 Flash Lite) vs LiSA 0.66/0.71 and TopicGPT 0.60/0.70; P1 0.73 vs 0.74 for TopicGPT and LiSA.
Bills: P1 0.57, ARI 0.42, NMI 0.53 (2.5 Flash Lite) vs LiSA 0.57/0.40/0.51.
645 (Bills) and 562 (Wiki) LLM prompts vs at least 8,024 and 15,242 for document-level methods.
Removing context clusters lowers Wiki ARI from 0.71 to 0.63.
strengths: Uses the LLM only at cluster level, reducing prompts by over 92%.
Ablations show the value of context clusters and of starting from fine, pure clusters.

limitations.text: Depends on initial embedding quality (harder for very short texts); closed-source LLM raises contamination, stochasticity and reproducibility concerns.
Dataset sizes given for Bills (8,024) and Wiki (15,242) appear swapped relative to the common test splits used by other papers (Wiki test 8,024, Bills test 15,242).
Wiki P1 is not the best (0.73 vs 0.74).
